rivet:grass.description: The grassy surface of temperate terrain. Breaking it gives [Dirt](Item-dirt.md).
rivet:grass.obtain: Find it on the surface. Mining drops dirt, so use the Creative catalog to obtain the grass block item.

rivet:dirt.description: A common building block and the base material for farmland.
rivet:dirt.obtain: Dig dirt or grassy ground with your hands; a shovel makes digging faster.
rivet:dirt.use: Use a [hoe](Item-wood-hoe.md) on exposed dirt or grass to make [Farmland](Item-farmland.md).

rivet:stone.description: The solid rock beneath the surface. Mining it drops [Cobblestone](Item-cobblestone.md); smelting cobblestone makes a placeable stone block.

rivet:log.description: Wood from tree trunks. It starts the plank, tool and charcoal crafting chains.
rivet:log.obtain: Break a tree trunk with your hands, or use an axe for faster chopping and upward tree felling.

rivet:leaves.description: Leaf blocks form tree canopies and can be used for foliage decoration.
rivet:leaves.obtain: Break leaves in a tree canopy. Hoes and blades make clearing leaves faster.
rivet:leaves.use: Mining natural leaves retains the leaf block and may also drop a [Sapling](Item-sapling.md) (5%) and/or an [Apple](Item-apple.md) (2%). Natural leaves also roll these drops when decaying after trunk removal. Player-placed leaves never produce bonus drops.

rivet:starter_axe.description: Legacy equipment retained for historical test fixtures. Ordinary Survival expeditions start empty-handed and use the wood-to-diamond tool progression.
rivet:starter_axe.obtain: Available from the Creative catalog. Its old starter recipe is not part of the active recipe registry.

rivet:starter_pickaxe.description: Legacy equipment retained for historical test fixtures. Ordinary Survival expeditions start empty-handed and use the wood-to-diamond tool progression.
rivet:starter_pickaxe.obtain: Available from the Creative catalog. Its old starter recipe is not part of the active recipe registry.

rivet:starter_dagger.description: Legacy equipment retained for historical test fixtures. Ordinary Survival expeditions start empty-handed and use the wood-to-diamond tool progression.
rivet:starter_dagger.obtain: Available from the Creative catalog. Its old starter recipe is not part of the active recipe registry.

rivet:coal_ore.description: Black coal pockets in lighter fractured host rock. A finite underground deposit found at **Y 0 to 80**, with the strongest generation preference near **Y 40**. These are world heights, not depth below the surface. Ore replaces stone and does not regenerate after mining.

rivet:copper_ore.description: Orange copper seams and pockets in fractured dark stone. A finite underground deposit found at **Y −48 to 64**, with the strongest generation preference near **Y 16**. These are world heights, not depth below the surface. Ore replaces stone and does not regenerate after mining. Mining drops one [Raw Copper](Item-raw-copper.md) with this same stylised ore-block appearance, ready for smelting or crushing.

rivet:iron_ore.description: Silver-grey mineral pockets in fractured dark stone. A finite underground deposit found at **Y −160 to 48**, with the strongest generation preference near **Y −48**. These are world heights, not depth below the surface. Ore replaces stone and does not regenerate after mining. Mining drops one [Raw Iron](Item-raw-iron.md) with this same stylised ore-block appearance, ready for smelting or crushing.

rivet:gold_ore.description: Golden seams and pockets in fractured dark stone. A finite underground deposit found at **Y −240 to −64**, with the strongest generation preference near **Y −160**. These are world heights, not depth below the surface. Ore replaces stone and does not regenerate after mining.

rivet:diamond_ore.description: Green-tinted turquoise crystal pockets in fractured dark stone. A finite underground deposit found at **Y −255 to −160**, with the strongest generation preference near **Y −224**. These are world heights, not depth below the surface. Ore replaces stone and does not regenerate after mining.

rivet:azure_ore.description:
Dark fractured stone threaded with bright blue crystal seams. A finite underground deposit found at **Y −96 to 8**, with the strongest generation preference near **Y −40**. These are world heights, not depth below the surface. Ore replaces stone and does not regenerate after mining. Smelt the mined ore into an [Azure Crystal](Item-azure-crystal.md).

![Azure ore seams in a natural underground deposit](images/azure-natural-deposit.png)

![The Azure ore model held in game](images/azure-held.png)

rivet:bedrock.description: The protected base of the world at **Y −256**. It stops hand mining, tools and drills.
rivet:bedrock.obtain: Occurs naturally at the world floor. It cannot be mined or collected in Survival. Its registered catalog entry is not a placeable item.

rivet:raw_iron.description: Silver-grey mineral pockets in fractured stone: mined iron keeps the stylised ore-block appearance on the ground, in your hand and in the inventory. Smelt one directly for one ingot, or use a [Crusher](Item-crusher.md) to make two crushed pieces and smelt those for two ingots. Raw ore items cannot be placed back as terrain.

rivet:raw_copper.description: Orange mineral pockets in fractured stone: mined copper keeps the stylised ore-block appearance on the ground, in your hand and in the inventory. Smelt one directly for one ingot, or use a [Crusher](Item-crusher.md) to make two crushed pieces and smelt those for two ingots. Raw ore items cannot be placed back as terrain.

rivet:raw_gold.description: Raw metal obtained from an ore deposit. Smelt it directly for one ingot, or use a [Crusher](Item-crusher.md) to make two crushed pieces and smelt those for two ingots. Raw ore items cannot be placed back as ore blocks.

rivet:coal.description: A mined fuel and torch ingredient. It powers a [Furnace](Item-furnace.md) or [Boiler Engine](Item-boiler-engine.md) and is also used to craft batteries.

rivet:diamond.description: A deep-mined gem used for the highest current tool tier and armor. It can also be packed into storage blocks.

rivet:planks.description: Processed wood for early tools, sticks, stations and building. One log makes four planks.

rivet:stick.description: A wooden handle used in tools and torches. Two planks arranged vertically make four sticks.

rivet:cobblestone.description: Rough stone used for stone tools, furnaces and construction. Smelting it produces [Stone](Item-stone.md).

rivet:workbench.description: A placed crafting station with a **3×3 grid** for tools, armor, storage and the first Machinist’s Bench.
rivet:workbench.use:
Place it, then press **E or right-click** to open it. The workbench can also make personal 2×2 recipes. See the [crafting guide](Crafting-Recipes.md) for the first steps.

A wooden carpenter’s bench with iron-bound trestles, a vise and hand tools.

![Placed workbench in the game](images/starter-workbench.png)

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:furnace.description: A fuel-burning station for smelting ore, making charcoal and glass, and cooking potatoes.
rivet:furnace.use:
Place and open it with **E or right-click**. Add an input, add fuel separately, and collect the output. Fuel continues burning after ignition even if input runs out. The recipes below list processing time and accepted fuels.

A stone furnace with a recessed arched firebox. The embers glow while fuel is burning and go dark when it runs out.

![Placed furnace in the game](images/starter-furnace.png)

Connect [Item Pipes](Item-item-pipe.md) on any face. Blue Input at the back accepts fuel only; the other five faces accept smeltable ingredients only. Rear-fed logs burn as fuel, while logs entering another face become charcoal. Red Output takes finished products only. Use a [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) to set each end. See [the crusher → furnace setup](Pipes.md#example-crusher--furnace--chest).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:chest.description: A placed container with **27 inventory slots**.
rivet:chest.use:
Open with **E or right-click** to store items. An [Extractor](Item-extractor.md) can move items from a chest into [Item Pipe](Item-item-pipe.md). An [Inventory Sensor](Item-inventory-sensor.md) can monitor its contents.

A wooden storage chest with an iron-banded lid and brass latch.

![Placed chest in the game](images/starter-chest.png) Item Pipes can connect on every face. A selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) sets each chest-facing pipe end to blue Input (store) or red Output (supply). See [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:charcoal.description: Wood converted into fuel. It works as an alternative to coal in torches, furnaces and boiler engines.

rivet:potato.description: A food item and planting material. Eat it raw for 1 food point, or bake it for 5.
rivet:potato.obtain: Harvest naturally occurring ripe potatoes on grassy terrain, or grow your own crop. A ripe crop yields **2–4 potatoes**; an immature crop returns **one potato**, which you can eat or replant.
rivet:potato.use: Till grass or dirt with a hoe, then use one potato on the exposed [Farmland](Item-farmland.md). Each of the three growth stages takes 60 seconds while suitable exposed terrain is loaded. Water irrigation is not required by the current crop system.

rivet:baked_potato.description: Cooked food that restores **5 food points**, compared with 1 for a raw potato. Baked potatoes cannot be planted.

rivet:farmland.description: Tilled soil for potatoes, wheat, flax, carrots and berry plants.
rivet:farmland.obtain: Use a [hoe](Item-wood-hoe.md) on grass or dirt with open space above it. Farmland is made in the world, not crafted or placed as an inventory block.
rivet:farmland.use: Select the planting item and right-click farmland. Keep crops exposed and their terrain loaded. No watering is required; see [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:potato_plant_0.description: Potato seedlings are stage 1 of the potato crop. Harvesting early returns **one potato** for eating or replanting; wait until ripe for **2–4 potatoes**.
rivet:potato_plant_0.use: After 60 seconds under suitable conditions, this becomes [Young potatoes](Item-potato-plant-1.md). Crop stages are world states, not placeable inventory plants.

rivet:potato_plant_1.description: Young potatoes are stage 2 of the potato crop. Harvesting early returns **one potato** for eating or replanting; wait until ripe for **2–4 potatoes**.
rivet:potato_plant_1.obtain: Let [Potato seedlings](Item-potato-plant-0.md) grow for 60 seconds on suitable loaded, exposed terrain.
rivet:potato_plant_1.use: After 60 seconds under suitable conditions, this becomes [Flowering potatoes](Item-potato-plant-2.md). Crop stages are world states, not placeable inventory plants.

rivet:potato_plant_2.description: Flowering potatoes are stage 3 of the potato crop. Harvesting early returns **one potato** for eating or replanting; wait until ripe for **2–4 potatoes**.
rivet:potato_plant_2.obtain: Let [Young potatoes](Item-potato-plant-1.md) grow for 60 seconds on suitable loaded, exposed terrain.
rivet:potato_plant_2.use: After 60 seconds under suitable conditions, this becomes [Ripe potatoes](Item-potato-plant-3.md). Crop stages are world states, not placeable inventory plants.

rivet:potato_plant_3.description: Ripe potatoes are stage 4 of the potato crop. Harvest for **2–4 potatoes**.
rivet:potato_plant_3.obtain: Find wild ripe crops on grassy ground, or let flowering potatoes finish growing.
rivet:potato_plant_3.use: Use harvested potatoes for food or replanting.

rivet:sand.description: A pale building material that can be smelted into [Glass](Item-glass.md).
rivet:sand.obtain: Gather sand from sandy terrain, including desert surfaces and water beds, or crush one [Stone](Item-stone.md) or [Cobblestone](Item-cobblestone.md) into one sand in a powered [Crusher](Item-crusher.md).

rivet:snow.description: A white surface block used for building.

rivet:red_clay.description: A red building block from badlands terrain.
rivet:red_clay.obtain: Gather it from exposed red clay in the badlands.

rivet:bucket.description: An empty container for moving one water or lava source, equivalent to **10 L**.
rivet:bucket.obtain: Craft it from iron ingots, or empty a [Water bucket](Item-water-bucket.md) or [Lava bucket](Item-lava-bucket.md).
rivet:bucket.use: Use it on a source cell to collect the liquid; flowing cells cannot be collected. Filling and emptying replace the same inventory slot. See [Lava](Lava.md) for deep lakes and burning hazards, or [Pumps and water](Pumps-and-water.md) for renewable water.

rivet:water_bucket.description: A bucket holding one water source, equivalent to **10 L**.
rivet:water_bucket.obtain: Use an empty [Bucket](Item-bucket.md) on source water, or remove 10 L through a filled machine’s bucket controls. This is a fluid transfer, not a grid recipe.
rivet:water_bucket.use: Use it to place source water in the world, or add 10 L through a boiler or tank interface. Emptying it returns a [Bucket](Item-bucket.md). See the [renewable pool guide](Pumps-and-water.md). Water also extinguishes a player who is [burning after lava contact](Lava.md).

rivet:torch.description: A recoverable light source that attaches to a solid block’s top or side. Coal and charcoal recipes each produce four torches.
rivet:torch.obtain: Craft it using either recipe below.
rivet:torch.use: Select a torch in your hotbar to cast warm light around you as you explore, or place it on a supported top or side face to light the area. Switching items or using the last held torch turns off the carried light. Removing a placed torch’s support drops it; water can wash it away. Held and placed torches do not burn fuel or need electricity.

rivet:azure_crystal.description: A smelted industrial material used in the Machinist’s Bench, Blue Signal parts and other assemblies.

rivet:copper_wire.description: Drawn copper used in electrical cables, signals and machine assemblies.

rivet:copper_plate.description: A shaped copper component for fluid equipment, tanks and other assemblies.

rivet:iron_plate.description: A shaped iron component for machine casings, structural parts and assemblies.

rivet:cog.description: An iron mechanical component used in machines and item extraction.

rivet:rivets.description: Small iron fasteners used in industrial and multiblock assemblies.

rivet:machine_casing.description: The common frame used to assemble machinery and batteries.

rivet:glass.description: Smelted sand used as a component in lamps, tank windows and controllers. This glass item is not a standalone placeable window block.

rivet:tank_frame.use:
Use this part in a sealed hollow tank. The [tank construction guide](Tanks.md) gives the shopping list, layer diagrams, outward-facing controls and repair instructions.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:tank_wall.use:
Use this part in a sealed hollow tank. The [tank construction guide](Tanks.md) gives the shopping list, layer diagrams, outward-facing controls and repair instructions.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:tank_glass.use:
Use this part in a sealed hollow tank. The [tank construction guide](Tanks.md) gives the shopping list, layer diagrams, outward-facing controls and repair instructions.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:tank_controller.use:
Use exactly one outward-facing controller in a sealed [multiblock tank](Tanks.md). Mining retains all stored liquid and capacity in the recovered controller. Recovery Out allows red Output pipe ends on its exposed faces to drain even a breached tank; a blue Input end never fills a recovery controller. Select a [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) to configure the pipe end. See [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

Accepts any registered liquid, including lava, one type at a time. Mining keeps its exact liquid; filled items each use one slot and empty ones stack normally. Shift-left-click with one in hand to discard its liquid. See [tank recovery and controls](Tanks.md#repairs-and-dismantling).

rivet:tank_port.use:
Use this part in a sealed [multiblock tank](Tanks.md), facing outward for formation. Enable its port in the interface; attach Fluid Pipe on an accessible face and use a selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) to choose blue Input or red Output at each end. See [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:tank_hatch.use:
Use this part in a sealed hollow tank. The [tank construction guide](Tanks.md) gives the shopping list, layer diagrams, outward-facing controls and repair instructions.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:tank_valve.use:
Use this part in a sealed [multiblock tank](Tanks.md), facing outward for formation. Enable its port in the interface; attach Fluid Pipe on an accessible face and use a selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) to choose blue Input or red Output at each end. An attached ON [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) is also required; OFF or missing signal keeps the valve closed. See [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:tank_sensor.use:
Use this part in a sealed hollow tank. The [tank construction guide](Tanks.md) gives the shopping list, layer diagrams, outward-facing controls and repair instructions.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:signal_wire.use:
See [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) for connection directions and control examples. Signal carries an ON/OFF instruction; machines still need their separate resources and electricity.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:signal_conduit.use:
See [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) for connection directions and control examples. Signal carries an ON/OFF instruction; machines still need their separate resources and electricity.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:signal_relay.use:
See [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) for connection directions and control examples. Signal carries an ON/OFF instruction; machines still need their separate resources and electricity.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:lever.use: See [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) for connection directions and control examples. Signal carries an ON/OFF instruction; machines still need their separate resources and electricity.

rivet:button.use: See [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) for connection directions and control examples. Signal carries an ON/OFF instruction; machines still need their separate resources and electricity.

rivet:signal_indicator.use:
See [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) for connection directions and control examples. Signal carries an ON/OFF instruction; machines still need their separate resources and electricity.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:workshop_hatch.use:
See [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) for connection directions and control examples. Signal carries an ON/OFF instruction; machines still need their separate resources and electricity.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:inventory_sensor.use:
See [Blue Signal](Blue-Signal.md) for connection directions and control examples. Signal carries an ON/OFF instruction; machines still need their separate resources and electricity.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:power_cable.use:
Connect to any of the six faces of generators, powered machines or eligible batteries. Electricity flows automatically; it has no wrench direction setting. Bank member cells are disconnected while claimed, so use the bank controller. See [Electricity and batteries](Electricity-and-batteries.md) and [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

For boiler generation, connect this cable to the **Alternator**, not the boiler’s mechanical shaft. The boiler needs a directly adjacent, correctly aligned alternator to generate electricity. See [the illustrated setup](Electricity-and-batteries.md#why-running-can-still-mean-zero-electricity).

rivet:alternator.use:
Place immediately on the Boiler Engine’s right with the shafts meeting. Electrical cables can connect on any of its six faces. See [Electricity and batteries](Electricity-and-batteries.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

This is the electrical generator in a boiler setup. It supplies **800 W** only when its left shaft directly meets the right shaft of an eligible running boiler; both machines must face the same direction. A cable, pipe or gap between the machines prevents coupling. The boiler can still burn fuel without this connection. See [the complete generation route](Electricity-and-batteries.md#check-the-complete-route).

rivet:boiler_engine.use:
Supply coal/charcoal and water manually, or use rear Item Pipe fuel input and Fluid Pipe water input on any face. Use a selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) to set blue input arrows. Its right-hand mechanical shaft must still meet an [Alternator](Item-alternator.md). See [Pipes](Pipes.md) and [Electricity](Electricity-and-batteries.md). Item Pipe supplies coal or charcoal only through the back, relative to placement rotation. Water pipes can enter any face.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

**Running means shaft power, not electricity.** This boiler has no electrical output and continues consuming fuel and water even without an alternator or electrical demand. Place a separate [Alternator](Item-alternator.md) immediately on its right, facing the same direction, with shafts meeting. Connect Power Cable to the alternator. See [why Running can still mean zero electricity](Electricity-and-batteries.md#why-running-can-still-mean-zero-electricity), with an actual missing-alternator example.

rivet:workshop_lamp.use:
Connect electricity on any face; it needs **20 W**. Front Blue Signal control is optional. See [Electricity and batteries](Electricity-and-batteries.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:battery_block.use:
Crafted and Creative-catalog blocks start **empty**. Recovered blocks keep their charge. Stores **100 kJ**, captures all surplus while it has room and supplies connected demand while it has charge. Separate cable grids can charge and draw from the same battery simultaneously. Mining keeps the cell’s charge. See [batteries and battery banks](Electricity-and-batteries.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md). Batteries on the same grid share surplus charging and deficit discharge equally, skipping full or empty cells.

If a boiler burns fuel but this battery receives **0 W**, check for a separate, correctly coupled alternator. A cable attached directly to the boiler cannot charge it. See [boiler and battery troubleshooting](Electricity-and-batteries.md#why-running-can-still-mean-zero-electricity).

Mining keeps its exact charge, including in a bank. Charged blocks each use one slot; empty blocks stack normally. Shift-left-click with one in hand to discard its charge. Chests, item pipes, drops, re-placement and saves retain the charge. See [recovery controls](Electricity-and-batteries.md).

rivet:battery_controller.use:
Place exactly one controller in a solid rectangular pack of battery blocks, with its front facing out. The controller adds no storage of its own. See the [battery bank guide](Electricity-and-batteries.md) for dimensions, wiring and charge-preserving repairs. Connect electricity to any exposed controller face; claimed member-cell sockets remain inactive.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md). A formed bank counts as one endpoint when sharing grid power with other batteries.

rivet:pump.use:
Position it one block **above** source water. It requires **no electricity**. Attach Fluid Pipe on a free face; use a selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) to set the pump-facing end to red Output. Keep the cell directly below free for source water. One extraction moves 10 L in two eligible seconds. Optional Blue Signal can pause it; pumping can start and recover boiler generation during a blackout. See [Pipes](Pipes.md) and the [renewable pool guide](Pumps-and-water.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:water_tank.use:
Stores **100 L** in one block. Use bucket controls or Fluid Pipes on any face. With a selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md), right-click each tank-facing pipe end to set blue Input or red Output. Separate ends keep separate settings. See [Pipes](Pipes.md); for larger storage build a [multiblock tank](Tanks.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

Accepts any registered liquid, including lava, one type at a time. Mining keeps its exact liquid; filled items each use one slot and empty ones stack normally. Shift-left-click with one in hand to discard its liquid. See [tank recovery and controls](Tanks.md#repairs-and-dismantling).

rivet:item_pipe.use:
Connect any face of a supported item machine, furnace or chest. Select a [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) and right-click each machine-facing pipe end to cycle blue Input, red Output and No connection. Arrows show only while holding the wrench; No connection removes the arm, and clicking that side again reconnects it. A chest can supply items directly through an output end. Machines accept only compatible ingredients or fuel; rejected cargo stays at its source, and mixed chests can send other compatible stacks. Receivers prefer cargo matching their current input or output before starting another compatible type. Fuel-burning machines accept fuel only at the back and ingredients through other input faces. Machines without fuel requirements also accept ordinary input at the back. Furnaces can burn rear-fed logs to turn side-fed logs into charcoal and output only finished products. Open the pipe normally to add independent signal or power fittings. See [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md). Branched grids share compatible transfers equally; full destinations give their share to those with room. See [sharing a branched grid](Pipes.md#sharing-a-branched-grid).

rivet:fluid_pipe.use:
Connect any face of a water machine or functional tank fluid port. A selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) plus right-click on the machine-facing end cycles blue Input, red Output and No connection. Arrows show only while holding the wrench; No connection removes the arm, and clicking that side again reconnects it. Opening the pipe normally gives access to separate signal/power fittings. See [Pipes](Pipes.md) and [tanks](Tanks.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md). Branched grids share compatible transfers equally; full destinations give their share to those with room. See [sharing a branched grid](Pipes.md#sharing-a-branched-grid).

rivet:extractor.use:
Place a [Chest](Item-chest.md) on its left. Attach [Item Pipe](Item-item-pipe.md) on any free face, with a red Output arrow set using a selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md). It transfers up to four items per second and supports optional signal control. Direct chest-to-pipe output is also available; the Extractor adds signal control. See [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:crusher.use:
Connect power on any face. Use [Item Pipes](Item-item-pipe.md) on any face and a selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) to set blue ingredient inputs and red product outputs. Optional Blue Signal remains at the front. One raw copper, iron or gold makes two matching crushed pieces in five seconds at **160 W**. Smelt each piece in a [Furnace](Item-furnace.md). One [Stone](Item-stone.md) or [Cobblestone](Item-cobblestone.md) instead makes one [Sand](Item-sand.md), with the same time and power. See [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:drill.use:
Supply **240 W** on any face. It mines the finite column directly below and stops at protected bedrock. Attach Item Pipe on any face and use a selected [Wrench](Item-wrench.md) to set the drill-facing end to red Output. An attached OFF signal at the front disables it. See [Pipes](Pipes.md).

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:machinist_bench.use:
Place and open it with **E or right-click** for 4×4 crafting. It also accepts smaller crafting recipes. Industrial recipes are shapeless unless their page specifies a pattern; keep the required count in each occupied slot.

Opening its controls shows a matching illustration and name in the left panel. See [Machine interfaces](Machine-interfaces.md).

rivet:hand_crank.description: A manual generator for a small starting electricity reserve. It supplies 100 W during each half-second turn (50 J), using no fuel or water.
rivet:hand_crank.obtain: Craft at a 3×3 workbench from 2 copper ingots, 1 iron ingot, 1 stick and 2 planks.
rivet:hand_crank.use: Select it and right-click a battery side to attach it. Aim at the placed crank and right-click or press Interact for one turn; hold right-click to repeat. Connected loads use power first, then surplus charges eligible batteries. Power cables can connect on any face. See [Electricity and batteries](Electricity-and-batteries.md#starting-power-with-a-hand-crank).

rivet:sapling.description: A replantable young tree. Place it on dry grass or dirt to renew your wood supply.
rivet:sapling.obtain: Natural leaves have a 5% chance to drop one when destroyed or decayed after chopping a trunk. Mining or uprooting a planted sapling returns it.
rivet:sapling.use: Use on dry grass or dirt. After about three minutes of unpaused world simulation, it can grow into a broadleaf tree with 4–6 logs. The complete footprint needs loaded, clear space and geometric skylight. Buildings, water, foliage and characters postpone growth. Save/load preserves its deadline; time outside the game adds no growth.

rivet:apple.description: A ready-to-eat fruit restoring four food points (two food icons).
rivet:apple.obtain: Natural leaves have an independent 2% chance to drop an apple when destroyed, including decay after trunk chopping. Leaves on sapling-grown trees also qualify.
rivet:apple.use: Hold Use for 1.2 seconds to eat one. Releasing early cancels the bite; full hunger consumes nothing.

rivet:wrench.description: A reusable workshop tool for setting the direction of item and fluid pipe connections.
rivet:wrench.obtain: Craft one at a 3×3 [Workbench](Item-workbench.md) from three iron ingots in the shaped recipe below.
rivet:wrench.use: Select the Wrench in your hotbar and right-click (or Shift + right-click) the pipe end touching a compatible machine or chest. Each click cycles **Input (blue) → Output (red) → No connection → Input**. No connection removes the arm and blocks transfers at that end; wrench-click the same pipe side to reconnect. Arrows appear only while the Wrench is selected in your hand. The wrench is not consumed. Empty hands, other selected items and Interact cannot change direction. Pipe centres, pipe-to-pipe links and electrical cables have no direction to switch. See [Pipes](Pipes.md) for complete examples.

rivet:electric_furnace.description: Smelts and cooks the same recipes as the normal furnace using 200 W of electricity, with no item fuel.
rivet:electric_furnace.obtain: Craft at the Machinist’s Bench using one Furnace, one Machine Casing and four Copper Wire.
rivet:electric_furnace.use: Connect power on any face and open with right-click or Interact. Insert ingredients and collect output. Full power takes the same time as a normal furnace; shortages slow work. Pipes feed ingredients or extract products on any face. See the [Electric Furnace guide](Electric-Furnace.md) for setup.

rivet:lava_bucket.description: A bucket containing one lava source, equivalent to **10 L**.
rivet:lava_bucket.obtain: Use an empty [Bucket](Item-bucket.md) on source lava. New worlds have lava lakes near bedrock; see [Lava](Lava.md).
rivet:lava_bucket.use: Right-click a block face to place a source and recover your empty bucket. Lava flows slowly, never renews sources, destroys dropped items and burns players. It is safe while carried in inventory. A compatible multiblock tank can also accept or return 10 L through its bucket controls.

rivet:floater_rock.description: A magical rock that enables the Floater to hover. Used in remote workshop technology.
rivet:floater_rock.obtain: Kill a Floater to receive exactly one Floater Rock. Walk near the dropped rock to collect it. Floaters spawn on supported surfaces at night.
rivet:floater_rock.use: Craft [bridges and chunk loaders](Bridges-and-chunk-loaders.md) at the Machinist’s Bench. Combine one rock with a [Pump](Item-pump.md) to craft a [Ranged Liquid Pump](Item-ranged-liquid-pump.md); see [its setup guide](Ranged-Liquid-Pump.md).

rivet:ranged_liquid_pump.description: Collects liquid source blocks within eight blocks along each axis (a 17×17×17 cube), including lava. No electricity required.
rivet:ranged_liquid_pump.obtain: Combine one Pump and one Floater Rock at the Machinist’s Bench.
rivet:ranged_liquid_pump.use: See [Ranged Liquid Pump](Ranged-Liquid-Pump.md) for setup. Each source gives 10 L after two seconds of collection. Pipe it into a tank; the 10 L buffer holds one liquid at a time.

rivet:item_bridge.description: A Floater Rock bridge joining two distant item pipe networks.
rivet:item_bridge.obtain: Craft a pair at the Machinist’s Bench; see the recipe below.
rivet:item_bridge.use: Connect matching pipes/cables, then give both bridges the same private network name. Both chunks must be loaded. See [Bridges and chunk loaders](Bridges-and-chunk-loaders.md).

rivet:liquid_bridge.description: A Floater Rock bridge joining two distant liquid pipe networks.
rivet:liquid_bridge.obtain: Craft a pair at the Machinist’s Bench; see the recipe below.
rivet:liquid_bridge.use: Connect matching pipes/cables, then give both bridges the same private network name. Both chunks must be loaded. See [Bridges and chunk loaders](Bridges-and-chunk-loaders.md).

rivet:power_bridge.description: A Floater Rock bridge joining two distant electrical grids.
rivet:power_bridge.obtain: Craft a pair at the Machinist’s Bench; see the recipe below.
rivet:power_bridge.use: Connect matching pipes/cables, then give both bridges the same private network name. Both chunks must be loaded. See [Bridges and chunk loaders](Bridges-and-chunk-loaders.md).

rivet:chunk_loader.description: Keeps its own 32 × 32 × 32 chunk loaded and active while the world runs.
rivet:chunk_loader.use: Place to enable; Interact opens controls and shows chunk origin. No fuel/power required. Cover the full remote installation, including both bridge endpoints. Saves retain its enabled state. See [Bridges and chunk loaders](Bridges-and-chunk-loaders.md).

rivet:wheat_plant_0.description: Wheat plant, growth stage 1 of four.
rivet:wheat_plant_0.obtain: Find wild plants on grassy terrain or grow them from planting stock. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).
rivet:wheat_plant_0.use: Young plants return one planting item only. Mature plants yield resources and two seeds. Prepare farmland with a hoe to plant; no watering is required.

rivet:mushroom_plant_0.description: An edible mushroom cluster found on grassy terrain.
rivet:mushroom_plant_0.obtain: Explore newly generated terrain. Break a cluster to gather one or two mushrooms.
rivet:mushroom_plant_0.use: Forage only in this increment. Eat mushrooms raw or cook them in a [Cooker](Item-cooker.md).

rivet:wheat_seed.obtain: Harvest wild or cultivated wheat; young plants return one seed and mature plants return two.
rivet:wheat_seed.use: Select these seeds and right-click farmland prepared with a hoe. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:flax_seed.obtain: Harvest wild or cultivated flax; young plants return one seed and mature plants return two.
rivet:flax_seed.use: Select these seeds and right-click farmland prepared with a hoe. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:carrot_seed.obtain: Harvest wild or cultivated carrot; young plants return one seed and mature plants return two.
rivet:carrot_seed.use: Select these seeds and right-click farmland prepared with a hoe. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:berry_seed.obtain: Harvest wild or cultivated berry; young plants return one seed and mature plants return two.
rivet:berry_seed.use: Select these seeds and right-click farmland prepared with a hoe. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:grain.obtain: Harvest mature wheat plants. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:flax_fibre.description: Craft three fibres into one String.
rivet:flax_fibre.obtain: Harvest mature flax plants. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:carrot.description: Eat raw, roast it, or use it as a vegetable in stew.
rivet:carrot.obtain: Harvest mature carrot plants. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:berries.description: Eat raw or use as fruit in porridge.
rivet:berries.obtain: Harvest mature berry plants. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:mushroom.description: Eat raw, cook it, or add it to vegetable stew.
rivet:mushroom.obtain: Harvest mature mushroom plants. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md).

rivet:bread.description: Prepared food from a basic or electric cooker. Food never spoils.
rivet:bread.obtain: Select its recipe in a cooker and supply the listed ingredients plus fuel or electricity.
rivet:bread.use: Hold Use to eat. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md) for food values and ingredient alternatives.

rivet:string.description: Renewable flax cordage, crafted from three Flax Fibre.
rivet:string.use: Craft four Strings into one Cloth. Fishing rods are a later increment.

rivet:cloth.use: Begins the textile chain; beds are a later increment.

rivet:cooker.description: A food preparation station with selectable recipes and interchangeable tagged ingredients.
rivet:cooker.use: Right-click or Interact, select a recipe, load ingredients and supply burnable fuel. Rear pipes carry fuel; other faces accept ingredients. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md) for setup, recipes and screenshots. Partial work and stored heat persist through saves; blocked or idle cookers consume no new energy.

rivet:electric_cooker.description: A food preparation station with selectable recipes and interchangeable tagged ingredients.
rivet:electric_cooker.use: Right-click or Interact, select a recipe, load ingredients and supply 200 W electricity on any face. See [Farming and cooking](Farming-and-cooking.md) for setup, recipes and screenshots. Partial work and stored heat persist through saves; blocked or idle cookers consume no new energy.
